 E6 LINK INTERVENORS’ REPLY TO ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY
 LLC AND LCRA TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION’S RESPONSE TO
  MOTION FOR LEAVE TO FILE EXPERT DIRECT TESTIMONY AND EXHIBITS
                            OUT OF TIME



TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES:

       The E6 Link Intervenors ﬁle this Reply to Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC

and LCRA Transmission Services Corporation's Response and would respectfully show

as follows:




                                         1
                                 I.    INTRODUCTION

       1.     Oncor's response ignores the practical realities that gave rise to the Motion

for Leave and incorrectly portrays the requested relief as prejudicial. The facts

demonstrate the opposite.

       2.    The E6 Link Intervenors are aﬀected landowners and residents who

received notice only shortly before intervention and testimony deadlines. As explained

in the Motion for Leave, these residents had approximately thirty days to evaluate a

complex 765-kV transmission project, organize aﬀected property owners, retain counsel,

investigate route alternatives, locate and retain qualiﬁed experts, and prepare testimony

for ﬁling. Despite those extraordinary time constraints, Intervenors acted diligently and

in good faith throughout the proceeding.

       3.    The requested relief concerns the testimony of a single expert witness

addressing an issue central to the routing decision before the Commission. Admission of

that testimony will assist in the development of a complete evidentiary record and will

not unfairly prejudice any party.

 II.    THE INTERVENORS COMPLIED WITH PROCEDURE ESTABLISHED BY
                            THE ALJS

       4.     Oncor argues that the E6 Link Intervenors failed to timely indicate their

intent to oﬀer late-ﬁled testimony. That argument is directly contradicted by the language

of SOAH Order No. 6.




                                            2
       5.     The ALJs expressly provided that an intervenor who failed to ﬁle direct

testimony by May 13, 2026, would be dismissed as a party unless that intervenor, by May

20, 2026, ﬁled a response establishing good cause. The E6 Link Intervenors did exactly

that. The Motion for Leave was ﬁled on May 20, 2026, in accordance with the procedure

established by the ALJs.

      6.     Accordingly, the Intervenors did not ignore the procedural schedule or wait

until the eve of hearing to seek relief. Rather, they followed the precise mechanism

created by the ALJs for parties seeking relief from the May 13 deadline. Oncor's assertion

that the Intervenors failed to timely notify the Court of their circumstances is therefore

unfounded.

           III.      GOOD CAUSE EXISTS FOR THE REQUESTED RELIEF

      7.      Good cause exists for the reasons set forth in the Motion for Leave.

      8.     The E6 Link Intervenors were not parties who simply disregarded a

deadline. They were aﬀected residents who received notice and then had approximately

thirty days to investigate a highly technical proceeding involving a proposed 765-kV

transmission line.

      9.     During that limited period, counsel was required to:

              a. Organize numerous aﬀected landowners and residents;

              b. Evaluate route alternatives and project materials;

              c. Prepare and ﬁle testimony from multiple witnesses;



                                            3
               d. Identify and contact qualiﬁed experts;

              e. Determine whether potential experts had conﬂicts or had already been

                     retained by other parties in the proceeding; and

              f. Retain and prepare an expert capable of addressing the issues

                     presented.

      10.    The diﬃculty was not a lack of diligence. The diﬃculty was locating and

retaining an appropriately qualiﬁed expert within an extraordinarily compressed

timeframe. Once Dr. Carpenter was retained, Intervenors immediately began preparing

and ﬁling his testimony.

      11.    Under these circumstances, the Intervenors acted reasonably, diligently,

and in good faith.

              IV.      ONCOR’S CLAIM OF PREJUDICE IS MISPLACED

      12.     Oncor argues that admission of Dr. Carpenter's testimony would prejudice

other parties because the testimony was ﬁled after the original deadline.

      13.    The prejudice analysis should focus on the realities of this proceeding.

      14.    The aﬀected residents represented by the E6 Link Intervenors were

aﬀorded only approximately thirty days to retain counsel, locate and retain experts,

investigate route alternatives, gather evidence, prepare testimony, and participate in a

proceeding concerning a transmission project that had been planned and developed long

before they received notice. By contrast, Applicants and numerous participants



                                              4
 associated with other route segments have had the beneﬁt of extensive resources, retained

experts, and several months to evaluate, develop, and advocate their positions. Excluding

Intervenors' testimony under these circumstances would reward the very timing

constraints that limited their participation and would substantially prejudice the

residents most directly aﬀected by the proposed E6 Link.

      15.    More importantly, exclusion of the testimony would substantially prejudice

the Intervenors and the residents they represent by preventing the Commission from

considering expert testimony on an issue directly aﬀecting the routing decision.

      16.    Oncor identiﬁes no witness who became unavailable, no evidence that was

lost, and no hearing date that was impacted. The hearing schedule remains intact. The

testimony merely provides additional evidence relevant to a central issue already before

the Commission.

      17.    Any inconvenience claimed by Oncor pales in comparison to the prejudice

that would result from excluding relevant expert testimony from aﬀected residents who

had only thirty days to prepare their case.

     V.     THE TESTIMONY ADDRESSES A CENTRAL ROUTING ISSUE —
                        PRUDENT AVOIDANCE

      18.     Dr. Carpenter's testimony addresses the potential impacts associated with

locating a 765-kV transmission line in close proximity to residences and families.

      19.    Oncor adempts to characterize this testimony as introducing a new issue. It

does not.

                                              5
        20.    The Commission has long recognized that proximity to residences is an

important routing consideration. Indeed, the Commission's notice requirements

themselves demonstrate that reality. Landowners and residents located within speciﬁed

distances of a proposed transmission line are entitled to notice precisely because they are

among those most directly aﬀected by the project.

       21.    Likewise, the concept of prudent avoidance exists because the location of

high-voltage transmission facilities relative to homes and occupied structures is a

legitimate consideration in transmission line routing. The Commission's rules expressly

require consideration of whether a proposed route conforms with the policy of prudent

avoidance. 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101(b)(3)(B). The Commission deﬁnes prudent

avoidance as limiting exposures to electric and magnetic ﬁelds that can be avoided with

reasonable investments of money and eﬀort. 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.101(a)(6). Thus,

proximity to residences and resulting exposure concerns are not novel issues raised by

Intervenors; they are considerations expressly recognized by the Commission's own

routing criteria.

       22.    Oncor cannot simultaneously maintain that residents within close

proximity to a proposed transmission line must receive special notice because they are

uniquely aﬀected by the project while also arguing that expert testimony regarding those

impacts is somehow irrelevant or unfairly prejudicial.




                                            6
       23.     Moreover, this case involves a proposed 765-kV transmission line. The

existing transmission facilities in the area are not comparable in magnitude to the

proposed project. The testimony assists the Commission in evaluating whether routes

that place substantially more residences and families near a 765-kV facility impose

greater impacts than available alternatives.

      24.     That is precisely the type of evidence the Commission should consider

when making a routing determination.

    VI.      ADMISSION OF THE TESTIMONY WILL PROMOTE A COMPLETE
                           EVIDENTIARY RECORD

       25.    The Commission's routing decision will affect numerous landowners,

residents, and families for decades. Dr. Carpenter's testimony provides information

directly relevant to evaluating the impacts associated with competing route alternatives.

       26.    Texas administrative proceedings favor decisions based upon a complete

evidentiary record whenever doing so does not unfairly prejudice the rights of the

parties or disrupt the orderly administration of the proceeding.

       27.    Neither circumstance exists here.

       28.    The testimony concerns a central issue already before the Commission, does

not require modification of hearing dates, and will assist the Commission in evaluating

the relative impacts of competing routes. Excluding the testimony would deprive the

Commission of relevant evidence and unfairly prejudice the affected residents

represented by the E6 Link Intervenors.

                                               7
                                     VII.    PRAYER

       29.    WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, the E6 Link Intervenors

respectfully request that the Administrative Law Judges overrule Oncor's objections,

grant the Motion for Leave to File Expert Direct Testimony and Exhibits Out of Time,

admit Dr. Carpenter's testimony and exhibits into evidence, and grant such other and

further relief to which Intervenors may be justly entitled.




                                                 Respectfully submitted,

                                                 GRISSOM & THOMPSON, L.L.P
